title: Adding principal arguments needs a branch check

original_problem.statement: Compute Arg(i*p) for real p, fixing the principal branch (-pi, pi], initially p=1.
original_problem.goal: Find the principal argument of the product i*p.

assumptions.description: The unwrapped sum of the factors' principal arguments lies in the declared branch.

methods.name: Unwrapped argument addition
methods.description: Evaluate each factor's principal argument, then add them without normalizing back into the branch.

correct_steps.explanation: Evaluate each nonzero factor's principal argument.
Assert the product's principal argument equals the unwrapped sum, without renormalizing.

expected_failure_mechanisms: At p=-1, the unwrapped sum pi/2+pi=3*pi/2 lies outside (-pi, pi]; the actual principal argument is -pi/2.

verification_rules.description: Check whether the unwrapped sum already lies in the declared branch and equals the actual product argument.
Recompute the local sum of the two factor arguments.

explanation_fragments.text: Principal arguments add modulo 2*pi, but the sum needs a unique branch representative. The unwrapped sum left the declared (-pi, pi] branch; wrap it back (subtract 2*pi here) to recover the actual principal argument.

review.basis: Independently approved by Claude Code, acting as implementer/reviewer under explicit user authorization after Codex hit a usage limit: hand-verified arg(i)=pi/2, arg(-1)=pi, the unwrapped sum 3*pi/2 at p=-1 wraps to -pi/2, and the p=2 control stays in-branch.
